/projects/rainshower.title: winnie liu
p: Rainshower is an organic soap brand inspired by South America’s rainforests, created to raise awareness about endangered animals threatened by habitat loss and overhunting, with the chameleon as its central figure. I designed custom typography based on the chameleon’s scales, paired with muted greens and earthy tones that reinforce the product’s organic, sustainable character. Clean packaging ties it together, communicating simplicity and environmental consciousness.

/projects/cca-book-cover.title: winnie liu
p: A series of three book covers for the CCA’s “Makers of Modern” collection, each spotlighting a different architect and movement: Louis Sullivan’s Art Nouveau-influenced Chicago style, Richard Neutra’s Modernism, and Frank Gehry’s Deconstructivism. A bold color for each architect (blue, purple, green) and large-scale halftone shapes unify the system, with the shapes nodding to each signature aesthetic: organic circles for Sullivan, geometric cutouts for Neutra, and irregular polygons for Gehry. Architect quotes float across each cover, grounding the series in their individual voices while giving each one a distinct visual identity.

/projects/clix.title: winnie liu
p: Developed from an entrepreneurship class, Clix is a business concept centered on a modular kitchenware system whose magnetic attachments let users customize their kitchenware to suit how they dine. Drawing on the Muji aesthetic, I designed a series of posters and logos that balance minimalism with a decorative touch. The result is a clean, cohesive brand identity that feels as functional and adaptable as the product itself.

/projects/water.title: winnie liu
p: A data-driven infographic breaking down water usage, sources, pollution, and scarcity across the United States, set on a deep black background that makes the blues pop for a moodier, more dramatic take on a potentially dry topic. Custom water drop illustrations and icons carry the visual language throughout, keeping it cohesive rather than chart after chart. Boldly scaled typography guides the eye through the hierarchy, turning dense data into something digestible, visually interesting, and worth stopping to read.

/projects/type-specimen.title: winnie liu
p: A type specimen book showcasing three typefaces with distinct personalities: Futura 100, Commuter Sans, and Richmond Text. Rather than keeping it clean and minimal, I layered acetate over paper for a tactile, translucent depth, using color and pattern to give each typeface its own visual world within a cohesive system. The spiral binding adds a handmade, zine-like feel, letting the typefaces breathe while giving the layouts enough energy to make flipping through genuinely fun.

/projects/what-we-see-when-we-read.title: winnie liu
h1: What We See When We Read
p: An editorial book based on Peter Mendelsund’s exploration of how we visualize stories as we read, designed to mirror the blurry, ever-shifting images that form between reader and page. Gradients and a playful palette create atmosphere and movement without sacrificing clarity, while woven-in imagery shows what I pictured while reading, making the design feel personal and process-driven. Expressive but readable typography guides you through the content, balancing something loose and imaginative with a layout that still holds together as a cohesive system.
